hotspots.title: Salvini’s Roggero prison visit sparks outrage
hotspots.blurb: Matteo Salvini's high-profile visit to jailed jeweler Mario Roggero, convicted of double murder, has ignited a firestorm. The Lega leader's advocacy for Roggero's pardon and potential candidacy has drawn sharp criticism from opposition parties and legal experts, who accuse Salvini of politicizing a settled court case and undermining judicial authority.
hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to its moral and legal controversy, with Salvini's actions framed as a direct challenge to Italy's judicial system and a cynical ploy to rally far-right support ahead of elections.

hotspots.title: PiS’s internal feud over leadership intensifies
hotspots.blurb: Poland's ruling Law and Justice (PiS) party is embroiled in a bitter internal power struggle, with factions led by Jarosław Kaczyński and former Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki clashing over party direction. The conflict has escalated to the point of potential expulsions, with Kaczyński demanding loyalty and Morawiecki's allies resisting, threatening a party split ahead of the 2027 elections.
hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to its high-stakes leadership crisis, with the potential for a party split that could reshape Poland's political landscape and undermine the right's electoral prospects.

hotspots.title: Trump’s election fraud claims dominate coverage

hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to its high affective investment, with Trump's claims framed as a direct threat to U.S. democracy, evoking strong emotional responses from supporters and critics alike.

hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to its high affective investment, with the reforms framed as a radical shift in Hungary's economic policy, evoking strong reactions from both supporters and critics of the government.

hotspots.title: Farage’s Clacton by-election bid faces scrutiny
hotspots.blurb: Nigel Farage's decision to contest the Clacton by-election has drawn intense scrutiny, with critics accusing him of hypocrisy over his £5 million undeclared donation and questioning his commitment to the constituency. The record 34-candidate race, boycotted by major parties, has become a focal point for debates over Reform UK's credibility and Farage's political future.
hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to its high affective investment, with Farage's candidacy framed as a test of Reform UK's legitimacy and a potential turning point in British politics, evoking strong emotional responses from both supporters and critics.
